sentence: Der Forscher sagte, dass die Studentin den schwierigen Bericht gelesen hat.

values.pairing: Each finite I licenses the corresponding subject in Spec-IP.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The analysis adopts a DP version of X-bar Theory and the GB convention that subjects are base-generated in Spec-IP. Both clauses have head-final VP and I′ structures. The matrix verb selects the embedded CP as its propositional complement; dass occupies the embedded C position. Within that clause, gelesen heads VP, the accusative object precedes it, and the finite perfect auxiliary hat is generated in I. The adjective schwierigen is an AP adjunct to N′ inside the object DP, not a clause-level modifier. Matrix C is initially empty, and matrix I contains abstract finite past and agreement features. The inflected lexical form sagte is already present under V; this analysis does not decompose its spelling into separately realized morphemes. First, sagte assigns the reporting Agent role to Der Forscher and the propositional Content role to the dass clause. Second, gelesen assigns the reading Agent role to die Studentin and the Theme role to den schwierigen Bericht. Third, the two finite I heads license nominative Case on their respective subjects. Fourth, gelesen governs and assigns accusative Case to its object. These are two independent finite subjects: no control, raising, or PRO dependency is posited.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the head-final base structure and the embedded dass clause.

relations.relation: V-to-I head movement and finite-feature licensing

values.traceLicensing: The raised head antecedent-governs its V trace.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Sagte moves from the previously established matrix V position and adjoins to the immediately higher I head. Its source becomes an unpronounced V trace, and the pronounced occurrence is now inside the complex I head. The abstract finite past and third-person singular features remain unpronounced within that head. The V-to-I chain connects the raised verb with its governed source trace, preserving the predicate's original theta and complement relations while checking its finite form against I. This intermediate workspace is necessary because subsequent movement to C must proceed from I rather than skip it. No comparable movement is required for the embedded auxiliary: hat was generated in I, and the overt complementizer dass keeps that clause outside the matrix V2 derivation.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the matrix verb from V to I.

values.traceLicensing: The raised I head antecedent-governs its I trace; the lower V dependency is maintained through the I position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The complex I head established in the preceding stage moves to the empty declarative C position, leaving an unpronounced I trace. The lexical verb and the silent inflectional feature head are carried with it; there is no second independent movement of the lexical verb. The new I-to-C dependency antecedent-governs the I trace and extends the existing head-movement path from the theta-bearing V position through I to C. This local succession satisfies the Head Movement Constraint. The finite verb now occupies the matrix left bracket, but Spec-CP is still empty, so the matrix subject remains after the verb at this intermediate point. The embedded dass clause stays in the matrix verb's original complement domain; its postverbal surface position will therefore not require extraposition.
derivationStages.statement: Move the finite matrix head from I to C.

relations.relation: subject A′ movement to the prefield

values.traceLicensing: The fronted subject antecedent-governs its Spec-IP trace.

values.configuration: One constituent in Spec-CP precedes the finite verb in C.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Der Forscher moves from its established Spec-IP position to Spec-CP, leaving an unpronounced DP trace. This is A′ movement into the German prefield, not movement to a new theta position. The resulting chain retains the Agent interpretation and nominative Case licensed at its Spec-IP source, and the fronted DP antecedent-governs that trace. Prefield occupation does not by itself force a contrastive-topic interpretation. With one constituent in Spec-CP and sagte in C, the matrix clause satisfies V2; second position counts constituents, not individual words. The embedded clause remains complementizer-initial and verb-final, with the sequence object–participle–finite auxiliary. All pronounced terminals now appear in exactly the supplied order. The comma and final period in the displayed sentence have no separate terminals because neither is included in the supplied token list.
derivationStages.statement: Front the matrix subject and complete the subject-initial V2 sentence.
